sections.brief: The Justice Department's order of 21 November 1962 to the American Zionist Council. Open in one sentence from Volume II ([scene:s07g|From AZEC to AIPAC]), which already tells the AZEC→AZC→AZCPA lineage and the bare order; do not retell it. Go deeper: what FARA required in 1962 (registration within ten days, disclosure not prohibition, the penalties, from the research), the order's basis in Jewish Agency money (more than $5 million over eight years in the order; $5,100,001.02 for 1 January 1955–31 December 1962 in the scene) and the Council's fight as Smith reports it (Rifkind, 'choke the very life', Lenvin, the Wall Street Journal report, the October 1963 FBI offer), each attributed to Smith or Arikat as reported, not as primary fact. Then set out which body was which in 1962: the scene and fis_s06 say AIPAC was restructured or incorporated in early 1963, while Kenen (speaking in September 1963), Barda and Wikipedia date the committee to 1951/1953/1954 and the AIPAC name to 1958 or 1959; present both, say what each dates, and do not resolve beyond the sources. Present the dispute over whether the Council ever registered (the 2016 Wikipedia snapshot against every other source). Tell fis_s06 only for 1962–63 and link forward for 1988 and 2024. Figure: timeline November 1962–October 1963 from the research; a comparison of the two accounts of AIPAC's origin.

The terms of the relationship at the turn of 1962–63, starting where Stage Four leaves the Hawk decision and the September 1962 visit (one sentence, link back). The 24 October 1962 circular reporting 'no evidence' and its instruction not to tell Tel Aviv; the editors' word 'fiasco' for the September visit; the Palm Beach meeting with Golda Meir on 27 December 1962 ('special relationship', support 'in case of an invasion', the limit that it could not harm ties with Arab states, Meir's reassurance on the reactor). Use the aid panel aid_arms:Overview:2 ('1962 First US military aid — as loans') and discuss it with Kenen's figures (Hawk loan of about $25 million over ten years; aid of about $85 million in 1963), flagged as his figures from an OCR text. Link wa_s07 in one sentence for the long-run case for the alliance; do not draw its 2020s material. Figure: key figures (fig-stats) for 1962–63.

How Washington's view of Dimona hardened between January and May 1963, in document order: NIE 30-63 (23 January; one or two weapons a year at full power), Thomas's 1 February proposal, the embassy airgram A-517 of 13 February ('not making a serious effort'), Komer's '67-68' warning, Sherman Kent's 6 March memorandum (each of its four judgments), NSAM 231 of 26 March (and the discrepancy in its addressees), SNIE 30-2-63 of 8 May (device late 1965, more likely 1966; deliverable 1967–68), and Kennedy's remarks to Couve de Murville on 25 May in both the French and US records. Present the dispute between the embassy's and the estimates' readings, and separate capability from intent throughout, as the estimates themselves do. Name Kennedy's stated motive (proliferation as a challenge to American power; drawing in the Soviets) without inferring more. Figure: timeline of the estimates and directives.

The Senate inquiry as a whole, before Part 9: S. Res. 362 and S. Res. 26 (the mandate's wording, 1 March 1963–31 January 1964, the $48,600 cap, the reporting deadline, subpoena power), and the thirteen published parts with their subjects (Philippine and Dominican sugar, the Dominican Information Center and INS, the Hamilton Wright Organization for the Republic of China and South Africa, Selvage and Lee for Portuguese interests, Davidson for Somoza, Julius Klein for West German interests), so the reader sees the Jewish Agency as Part 9 of a wider investigation. Then the Act's administration from the Attorney General's report: 419 and 480 active registrations, no prosecutions in 1964, more than 200 amended statements, the Jewish Agency–American Section as an existing registrant distributing The Israel Digest (8,500), the proposed separate-books rule and Rabinowitz v. Attorney General. Present the dispute over whether the Agency was one case among many or a case of special weight, with Smith's and Barda's readings labelled. Figure: comparison table of the parts (principal, agent, part); key figures from the 1964 report.

The battle of the letters, 27 March–15 June 1963, from the declassified texts: telegram 658, Barbour's 2 April meeting, Peres at the White House the same day with both records of his assurance and the editors' point that 'not do anything' and 'not introduce' differ; Talbot's 4 April démarche; the Arab Federation Proclamation of 17 April and Ben-Gurion's 26 April letter; Kennedy's 4 May reply; Ben-Gurion's 12 May letter ('another Holocaust', the security agreement, arms parity, a demilitarized West Bank) stated fairly as Israel's case in its own terms; Komer's 'good opening bid'; Kennedy's 17/19 May letter and the 'seriously jeopardized' sentence; the 27 May reply; the Brubeck schedule; the undelivered 15 June letter. Where the scene states background (the 1958 U-2 'discovery', the December 1960 Knesset statement), do not retell it: link back to Stage Four, whose research dates the discovery, and follow its dates if they differ from the scene's. NIE 30-63 is dated 23 January 1963. Present the 'ultimatum or not' dispute from both sides. Kennedy's refusal of an explicit guarantee belongs here. Tell the 1964–65 inspection material in the scene's last entity only as a forward link to [scene:s11d|Johnson's inspections]. Figure: timeline of the letters; comparison of what Kennedy asked and what Ben-Gurion offered.

16 June 1963: Ben-Gurion's resignation and Eshkol's succession. State the date dispute (16 June in the documents; 15 June in the editors' introduction; 26 June as the end of term in Wikipedia's infobox, with the swearing-in of Eshkol's government left as unverified). Give each explanation with its source and its evidentiary weight: his own 'personal reasons'; Weitz's account of isolation and suspicion; the CIA's view that his German policy was a cause; Sapir and Galili, and Cohen's 'may have been triggered, in part', on Kennedy's pressure. Say plainly that no document shows the letters caused the resignation and that the undelivered 15 June letter is the only direct intersection. Close with what followed for Ben-Gurion (Lavon demand, Rafi in June 1965, the November 1965 defeat) in two sentences, linking forward.

Part 9: the Jewish Agency before the committee, May–August 1963. The closed sessions (Hammer and Boukstein, 28 June report), the opening of the funding inquiry (2 August 1963 by Kenen's affidavit), Hamlin's testimony and his line on subscriptions, the $38,000 for Near East Report subscriptions, Kenen's affidavit (23% peak share, AZC work ended July 1960, purchases ended 1962, $100 a week), and the newsletter's origins (25 January 1955 decision, print runs, the 1957 subscription push). Present the two disputes in full: the money (the $5.1 million figure against Barda's unsourced $1.5 million) and what the hearing showed (Neumann's 'no wrong doing' and Barda's 'absolute' separation against Smith's and the American Council for Judaism's conduit reading, with the Council's claims about executive session and the 1960 convention expenses marked unverified). Use Kenen's own off-the-record words of 13 September 1963. From fis_s07 tell only the 1963 position (the domestic-funding defence as AIPAC's legal basis) and link forward for 1988 and 2024. Figure: money chain (Jewish Agency American Section → AZC subscriptions → Near East Report → readers/Congress → who bore the cost), built only from the cited figures and labelled with both positions.

Eshkol's answer, July–September 1963: the 4 July telegram delivered on 5 July, his advisers' 'real ultimatum', the 17 July interim reply, the seven weeks of consultation and Barbour's report of a divided cabinet, Eshkol's 'would do what it had to do', the 19 August reply (late-1963 visit before criticality, mid-1964 follow-up, no twice-yearly commitment), Kennedy's 26 August 'basic agreement', and the 16 September memorandum (the 'third visit', the plutonium separation plant, 'inclined to believe'). Then what became of it, briefly: criticality on 26 December 1963 by Israel's account against July 1963 on the IAEC website; the first visit on 18 January 1964 and the team's findings ($60 million, 20 tons of concentrate, 'ambitious project', the caveat that even intrusive visits could not prove peaceful use); the count of later visits (six against seven) and Cohen and Burr's later findings, stopping there and linking forward to cw6 and [scene:s11d|Johnson's inspections]. Present whether the agreement met Kennedy's demand from both sides. Figure: comparison of Kennedy's request and Eshkol's agreement.

Jewish dissent from Zionism in these years, so the reader sees that the FARA and 'peoplehood' questions were argued among American Jews themselves: the American Council for Judaism's origins (1942, 36 rabbis, Wolsey, Rosenwald, Berger), its post-1948 programme, its welcome for the 1962 order (per Smith), and the spring 1964 exchange over 'Jewish peoplehood' (the State Department letter of 20 April 1964; the AZC's 'purely a spiritual and cultural one'; Halprin's letters to Talbot and the Mallison rebuttal). State the Council's own 1997 account as its own. Close with its decline after 1967 and Berger's ouster in 1968 in one sentence. Do not generalize about American Jews; name the organizations and individuals.

A Palestinian answer at the UN, 14 November 1963: Ahmad Shukairy before the Special Political Committee on the UNRWA report, in his own terms (six cents a day; 1,120,170 refugees by June 1963 as his figure; restoration of property; the Jewish Agency's 1951 figures; his use of the Fulbright inquiry) and the US representative's reply. Mark his characterizations as his, including 'genocide', and set his reading of the inquiry beside Neumann's. Keep to the meeting; his later role at the PLO's founding in 1964 belongs to Stage Six (one forward sentence).

22 November 1963, told as a fact of timing. Order: where each thread stood that week (the FARA order unenforced after the October FBI offer, as Smith reports; Dimona under the August agreement with the first visit not yet held); the assassination in one plain paragraph with the official inquiries named as the scene names them; what the record shows afterwards (the first visit on 18 January 1964 'may have been delayed', per the editors; Johnson continuing the inspection demand, per Cohen and Burr; enforcement that 'gradually falls apart' per Smith, with no document of a decision). Then the claims of a link, as claimed and unsupported, with who makes them: Barda documents that such claims circulate (citing the 2025 CAM report) and finds 'no evidence whatsoever'; Giraldi's and Arikat's timing statements, which assert a sequence and cite no causal evidence. Embed claim_checker:How to Check:0 and use its two questions (is the fact true; does it prove the conclusion) on the timing claim. No implied causation anywhere in the prose. Link forward to [scene:s11d|Johnson's inspections] and cw6.
